Identify user sequences against the barcoding library (step 11 of Tutorial 5)

Source: R/barcoding_identify.R
identify_barcoding_query.Rd

Classifies each query against the IdTaxa model of each locus of the library, or of the one declared, and answers locus by locus with the three states of the branch. It never combines loci into one answer.

Usage

identify_barcoding_query(
  query,
  locus = NULL,
  library_dir = file.path("11_barcoding", "4_library"),
  metrics_dir = file.path("11_barcoding", "11_metrics"),
  threshold_dir = file.path("11_barcoding", "9_threshold"),
  genus_only_loci = "rbcL",
  output_dir = file.path("11_barcoding", "10_identify"),
  run_name = "query",
  threshold = 60,
  min_overlap = 100L,
  seed = 1L,
  processors = 1L,
  sample = NULL,
  report = TRUE
)

Arguments

query

A FASTA or GenBank flat-file path (a GenBank record is named by its accession), a Biostrings::DNAStringSet or a named character vector of sequences.

locus

Character or NULL. Loci to test; NULL tests every locus of the library.

library_dir

Character. Directory of step 4, with the LIB_<locus>.fasta files.

metrics_dir

Character. Directory of step 10, with TABLE_barcoding_metrics_summary_idtaxa.csv.

threshold_dir

Character or NULL. Directory of step 9, with TABLE_barcoding_species_threshold_idtaxa.csv, written by sweep_barcoding_threshold(method = "idtaxa"): the species threshold of each locus (step 9). A row that IdTaxa names at species rank keeps the species only when its species confidence reaches that threshold; otherwise it is named at genus rank, with reason below_species_threshold, and keeps in species_idtaxa and species_confidence what IdTaxa reached. The value used is in the column species_threshold. Without the table, or for a locus it lacks, the species threshold is threshold, with a message.

genus_only_loci

Character. Loci that answer at genus rank only: a row of one of them that IdTaxa names at species rank, over its species threshold, is named at genus rank, with reason genus_only_locus, and keeps in species_idtaxa and species_confidence what IdTaxa reached. Defaults to "rbcL": on the library of this version, built from GenBank, the species answers of rbcL were right in 11 of 34 (single records, sets of records and plastomes), and its species threshold of step 9 is the floor of 60. character(0) lets every locus name a species.

output_dir

Character. Where the table and the model cache are written.

run_name

Character. Suffix of the output table, TABLE_barcoding_identify_<run_name>.csv.

threshold

Numeric. IdTaxa confidence threshold. Defaults to 60, the operating threshold of the validation folds.

min_overlap

Integer. Minimum length of the region to classify. Defaults to 100.

seed

Integer. Seed of the models and of the queries. Defaults to 1, as in Tutorial 5.

processors

Integer. Processors for DECIPHER::IdTaxa().

sample

Character or NULL. A name for the specimen when the sequences of query are several loci of one specimen: they are then one sample, with one report that reads them together. NULL (the default): each sequence is a sample of its own.

report

Logical. Write the identification report (report_barcoding_identification()). The run record RUN_<run_name>.csv is written in any case.

Value

Invisibly, the table of answers: one row per query and locus tested.

Details

For each locus:

  1. The whole query is tested against the 20-mers of the locus on both strands, with the rule of the rest of the branch (share of 0.15, ratio of 3). If it matches, it is classified as it is (path = "whole"). This is the path of a Sanger sequence.

  2. If it does not match and it is longer than 1.5 times the longest library sequence of the locus, the region of the query with the most 20-mer hits in a window of that width is cropped and tested again (path = "crop"). other_windows counts the other windows with at least half as many hits, since an inverted repeat or an rDNA array can hold more than one copy.

  3. The region is cut to the core of the locus, the span of alignment columns covered by half or more of its library sequences: beyond its first and last 20-mer of the core, the query keeps only as many bases as the core itself holds there (core_trimmed gives the bases removed). A segment held by one or two references only is left out, so it cannot name them.

  4. When IdTaxa assigns a genus (state 1 or 2) with 3 or more sequences in the locus, the region as it was before step 3 is cut to the core of that genus, with the same rule, and classified again if that is not the region already classified (genus_core_trimmed gives the bases removed from it). The core of a genus can be narrower than that of the locus (two long references of a genus of short sequences cannot then take the queries of its absent species) or wider (a genus whose sequences are all longer than the core of the locus keeps them).

  5. State 3 is returned with its reason: no_overlap (no match), short_overlap (a region shorter than min_overlap) or low_confidence (IdTaxa's genus confidence under threshold).

The model of each locus is IdTaxa trained on the whole library of the locus with a fixed seed, the same model as the outgroup control of step 8. It is cached in output_dir/models/ with the md5 of its library file and trained again only when the library or the seed change. Each query has its own seed, from seed, the locus and its identifier (the accession of a Genus_species|accession name, the whole name otherwise). The random state of the session is left as it was.

Each row carries, for its locus, the wrong-species rate of IdTaxa measured in step 10 with the species present (validation_ws_rate_species_present, scheme E) and absent (validation_ws_rate_species_absent, scheme G), when that table exists and was measured at the same threshold.

A locus whose library holds a single species cannot be trained: its rows are state 3 with reason single_species_library.

Raw reads (FASTQ) are not accepted: paired Illumina reads go to identify_barcoding_reads(), a genome assembly to identify_barcoding_assembly(). Aligned reads (BAM, CRAM, SAM) stop with the command that converts them to FASTQ.

See also

run_barcoding_controls(), sweep_barcoding_threshold(), summarise_barcoding_metrics().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
identify_barcoding_query("my_sequences.fasta")
identify_barcoding_query("my_plastome.fasta", run_name = "plastome")
} # }
